4	@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
5	+# Adding persisted state, jobs or email to Fizzy
6	+
7	+Use this when a change adds a migration, a model or a `User::Settings` attribute, a job, a mailer, or hooks new behavior onto `Notification`. Names, values and labels come from the request, and this skill never overrides them. It tells you where each part of such a change lives in this codebase and what must stay consistent.
8	+
9	+Lines marked **[ws]** are facts verified in this workspace's repository. Treat the rest as checks to run.
10	+
11	+## 1. Code you build on (read these before designing)
12	+
13	+- **[ws]** `app/models/user/settings.rb` (`User::Settings`, table `user_settings`) is reached through `user.settings` (`has_one` in `app/models/user/configurable.rb`). It is created `after_create ... unless: :system?`, so code that reads it must handle `nil`.
14	+- **[ws]** For enums on string columns, follow the convention: `enum :status, %w[ a b c ].index_by(&:itself), default: :a` (see `app/models/export.rb`, `app/models/access.rb`, `app/models/identity/access_token.rb`). For an allow-list validation, see `validates ... inclusion:` in `app/models/entropy.rb`.
15	+- **[ws]** Settings are updated in place, as in `app/controllers/my/timezones_controller.rb`: `Current.user.settings.update!(...)`. `config/routes.rb` already has `namespace :notifications do resource :settings end`, so `PATCH /notifications/settings` routes to `Notifications::SettingsController#update` without a new route. For a select field, follow `app/views/my/access_tokens/new.html.erb:20` (`form.select ..., {}, class: "input input--select"`).
16	+- **[ws]** `app/models/notifier.rb` keeps one `Notification` row per (user, card): it calls `create_or_find_by(user:, card:)` and, on repeat activity, `update!(source:, creator:, read_at: nil, unread_count: +1)`. There is a unique index on `notifications [user_id, card_id]`. "A new notification" therefore means a create **or** a source change on an existing row. The existing hook to copy is `app/models/notification/pushable.rb`: `after_save_commit :push_later, if: :source_id_previously_changed?`. Its eligibility check is `!creator.system? && user.active? && account.active?`.
17	+- **[ws]** `notification.payload` returns `Notification::{Event,Mention,Default}Payload` (`app/models/notification/*_payload.rb`), with `title`, `body` and `url`. Reuse it for any text that describes a notification.
18	+
19	+## 2. Jobs and mail: facts that change the design
20	+
21	+- **[ws]** `app/jobs/application_job.rb` prepends `AccountTenanted`. A job captures `Current.account` when it is **enqueued** and restores it when it runs. `ApplicationJob` does not discard on `DeserializationError` by default, so each job declares `discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError` itself.
22	+- **[ws]** `config/initializers/active_job.rb` sets `enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true`, so a job enqueued inside a transaction is held until commit.
23	+- **[ws]** `ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob` prepends `AccountTenanted` (`config/initializers/active_job.rb`) and includes `SmtpDeliveryErrorHandling` (`lib/rails_ext/action_mailer_mail_delivery_job.rb`, concern in `app/jobs/concerns/smtp_delivery_error_handling.rb`). That concern retries timeouts and server-busy errors and ignores bad-recipient errors. **Decision rule:** if your own job sends mail, either call `Mailer.x(...).deliver_later` from it, which keeps that handling, or include `SmtpDeliveryErrorHandling` in your job. A bare `deliver_now` inside a custom job silently drops both.
24	+- **[ws]** `ApplicationMailer` (`app/mailers/application_mailer.rb`) uses `layout "mailer"` and `append_view_path app/views/mailers`. Its `default_url_options` adds `script_name: Current.account.slug` only when `Current.account` is set. Mailer templates live in `app/views/mailers/<mailer_name>/<action>.{html,text}.erb`, as for the account, export, import and magic_link mailers, each of which ships both html and text.
25	+- **[ws]** `app/views/layouts/mailer.html.erb` already styles `.title`, `.subtitle`, `.card__title`, `.notification`, `.notification__author`, `.notification__board`, `.notification__details` and `.footer`. Use those classes and do not invent new CSS.
26	+- **[ws]** Recipient addresses follow `@user.identity.email_address` (see the existing mailers). `user.identity` can be nil for deactivated users (`User#deactivate` sets `identity: nil`).
27	+
28	+## 3. Schema contract: every place a migration must show up
29	+
30	+- **[ws]** Migrations use `ActiveRecord::Migration[8.2]` with `id: :uuid` and `t.uuid` foreign keys, and no FK constraints. The newest existing migration is `20260709120000_*`, so your timestamp must be later.
